 Updated Fri, Oct 23 2026 4:16 PM EDT Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Dow tumbles more than 600 points as oil prices rise and market sell-off hits most sectors
 Hugh Leask Lee Ying Shan Tobias Burns Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange during morning trading on Oct. 14, 2026 in New York City. Michael M. Santiago | Getty Images The Dow slid on Friday as a sell-off in tech in the prior session shifted to other areas of the market and U.S. oil prices topped $100 a barrel amid rising fears that the U.S.-Iran conflict would flare up again. 
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 652.82 points, or 1.23%, to settle at 52,215.16, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.52% to 7,623.68. The Nasdaq Composite lost 0.21% to close at 25,955.34.
 More defensive stocks came under pressure on Friday, with the consumer staples, utilities and healthcare sectors all lower. Dow component American Express fell more than 3% after announcing it was cutting about 5% of its global workforce , citing the need to "prepare for AI." Caterpillar also edged down about 2%, while Goldman Sachs lost more than 1%, adding pressure to the 30-stock index.
 On Thursday, many technology stocks had pulled back as traders assessed the impact of outsized corporate borrowing and rising rates on AI and other tech names. Microsoft ticked higher on Friday. However, chip stocks such as Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices made a stronger move, with gains of nearly 3% and almost 2%, respectively. 
 "For the last two weeks, investors have been sprinting from tech stocks and data center beneficiary stocks to safe stuff, and eventually, you run out of people willing to do that sprint, and that's what today looks like and feels like," Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management, told CNBC. 
 Ellerbroek added that tech companies' earnings have proven strong this season, giving investors a reason to embrace tech stocks and focus less on emotion-based flights to safety.
 "Emotion and fear play a really big role," the investor said. But, "we've gotten a few tech companies' [latest quarterly financial reports] and their earnings results have been good." 
 The 10-year Treasury yield was at around 4.999%, up more than 4 basis points on the day. The benchmark yield had fallen below the key 5% level on Thursday for the first time in a month as investors grew cautious about the massive borrowing that is underway to finance the building of AI data centers. 
 Oil prices also rose on Friday, further pressuring stocks. West Texas Intermediate futures were up 3.8% to settle at $103.27 per barrel. Brent crude prices rose 3.1% to end the session at $116.72 for the highest settle since April. The gains follow reports that the U.S. and Israel may be drawing up plans for renewed attacks on Iran as part of the regional war that started in late February. Iran has countered that it is prepared to strike back as well. 
 On the week, the S&P 500 lost 0.5%, and the Nasdaq shed 0.7%. The Dow gained 0.4% in the period.
 2 Hours Ago Stocks close lower on Friday
 The three major stock indexes ended Friday's session with losses. 
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 1.23%, or 652.82 points, to finish at 52,215.16. The S&P 500 ended down 0.52% at 7,623.68. The Nasdaq Composite closed down 0.21% at 25,955.34.
 —Liz Napolitano 
 3 Hours Ago Diesel costs drain discount retailer margins and could push prices higher
 Prices of gasoline and diesel fuel are displayed in downtown Los Angeles, California, US, Oct. 15, 2026. Mike Blake | Reuters Shares of discount retailers are lower today after analysts at Wells Fargo warned in a note that rising diesel prices could pressure profits through the second half of the year and into 2027.
 With third-quarter diesel prices up about 60% year-over-year, analysts estimate the average hit to operating margin will rise to about 27 basis points from 18 basis points in the second quarter. The drag on earnings per share is expected to more than double to 6.2%.
 Dollar Tree and Dollar General are down around 5% in midday trading while Five Below and TJX Companies are both down more than 1% on the day. Wells Fargo says Dollar Tree is the most exposed, historically seeing a larger drag than peers when diesel spikes. They estimate the higher fuel costs will weigh on third-quarter profit by about $25 million, or 50 basis points of margin.
 The increased costs could mean additional pressure on retail inflation.
 -- Nick Wells 
 4 Hours Ago Bank of America raises ServiceNow price target to $180 on AI traction
 Signage outside the ServiceNow headquarters in Santa Clara, California, US, on Thursday, Sept. 4, 2025. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Bank of America raised its price target on ServiceNow to $180, implying roughly 15% upside from Thursday's close.
 BofA analyst Tal Liani reiterated his buy rating ahead of the company's third-quarter earnings on October 28, citing growing demand for its artificial intelligence offerings. 
 "We believe ServiceNow's AI could see broader adoption and incremental spend, which should support durable revenue growth," Liani wrote in a Friday note.
 The bank's October CIO survey showed that nearly 36% of respondents expect to allocate more than 10% of their software budgets to AI, while nearly 55% said they were likely or very likely to use ServiceNow for back-office AI applications.
 The analyst expects third-quarter subscription revenue to grow nearly 21% year over year as IT, customer service, and security adopt new AI products and automation tools. 
 — Deena Zaidi 
 5 Hours Ago Uranium, Nuclear ETFs fall to 52-week lows; Exxon, Chevron reach all-time highs
 Uranium, nuclear and clean energy exchange-traded funds all fell to 52-week lows on Friday, while the largest fossil fuel producers in the nation touched all-time highs. 
 Global X Uranium ETF and Sprott Uranium Miners ETF both dropped to their lowest levels since June 2025, while the VanEck Uranium and Nuclear ETF was at its lowest since May 2025. Of the stocks inside those ETFs, Centrus Energy , Oklo , NuScale Power , Energy Fuels and BWX Technologies were also at 52-week lows Friday. 
 Clean energy ETFs saw losses, too. Invesco Solar ETF and Invesco WilderHill Clean Energy ETF were at their lowest since September and August last year, respectively, while individual stocks in the group, such as NextPower , Solv Energy , Rivian Automotive and Fluence Energy , also dropped to 52-week lows.
 Meanwhile, ExxonMobil , Chevron and ConocoPhillips all traded at all-time highs on Friday.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon ExxonMobil in past 12 months — Scott Schnipper, Gina Francolla 
 5 Hours Ago Goldman eyes Oracle's investor day as AI pressures mount
 The Oracle logo is displayed on a building at an Oracle campus on Sept. 10, 2025 in Redwood Shores, California. Justin Sullivan | Getty Images In a Friday note to clients, Goldman Sachs posed some key questions about hyperscaler Oracle's AI strategy as pressures mount on the AI trade and investors grow increasingly wary to part with capital.
 Analyst Gabriela Borges at Goldman said the conversation around Oracle is centering on monetization in proportion to capital expenditures; the sustainability of demand amid customer concentration; and the company's ability to execute despite political pressures facing the data center buildout.
 Borges has a buy rating on the stock and a price target of $206, implying upside of 64.1% compared to a closing price recorded as $125.54.
 Among the key risks to the company listed by Goldman are "intense capex investment cycle and financing needs."
 "Oracle has outlined a FY27 financing framework supported by roughly $20bn of equity issuance (ATM program, already executed), $20 – 25 bn of customer prepayments ($11 bn as of 1Q), ~$20bn of debt issuance (expected in 2HFY27), with the remainder funded through operating cash flow," Borges wrote.
 – Tobias Burns 
 6 Hours Ago The S&P 500's ex-AI is breaking away in October
 Stocks outside the AI trade are taking the lead.
 The S&P 500 Excluding AI index closed Thursday up 12.4% this year, edging out the S&P 500's roughly 12% gain. The gap has converged largely in October. 
 The ex-AI index is up about 6.6% in October, while the S&P 500, weighed down by concerns around AI financing, is down roughly 0.4%.
 The move suggests some leadership broadening beyond AI-linked mega cap names that have dominated in recent periods. By sector, Energy and Consumer Staples are each up double digits in October while Information Technology and Communication Services lead lower, each down more than 5%.
 -- Nick Wells 
 6 Hours Ago Morgan Stanley lowers price target on CoreWeave
 Morgan Stanley reduced its price target on CoreWeave to $70 from $99 Friday, citing mounting financial pressures the so-called neocloud company is facing. The new target still implies 26% upside from Thursday's close.
 Shares of CoreWeave, down 2% on Friday, have sold off over the past week amid investor fears over its massive artificial intelligence-rated debt. Its bond yields have also jumped, while the spread on its credit default swaps — which are insurance against default — has widened to levels generally considered distressed. 
 Morgan Stanley believes CoreWeave's execution has been solid and said it "remains the speed and scale leader in a crowded neocloud ecosystem."
 "However, growing financing uncertainty reduces visibility into the path to deploying existing contracted capacity and achieving 8 GW [gigawatts] (active) longer-term," said analyst Adam Wood, who maintained his equal-weight rating on the stock. 
 He sees a multitude of outcomes for CoreWeave's future financing, "though the most reasonable path forward would likely be through securing a portion of the financing via a hyperscaler agreement to obtain a more attractive rate."
 — Michelle Fox 
 7 Hours Ago Consumer sentiment flat in October as inflation fears edge higher
 Shoppers carry UNIQLO and Target bags in San Francisco, California, US, on Monday, Oct. 12, 2026. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Consumer sentiment changed little in October from historically low levels as inflation weighed on the economic outlook, according to a University of Michigan survey released Friday.
 The survey showed the headline consumer sentiment index at 48 for the end of the month, off just 0.1 point from September and better than the Dow Jones consensus for 46.3. Compared with a year ago, the gauge tumbled 10.4%.
 Current conditions sentiment declined 8.3% monthly but the expectations measure rose 5.4% and was off just 3% from the same period in 2025.
 On inflation, the one-year outlook rose to 4.7%, while the five-year expectation accelerated to 3.5%, both 0.1 percentage point higher than September.
 —Jeff Cox 
 8 Hours Ago Seaport is bearish on Nvidia, reiterating sell rating on AI leader
 Participants visit the NVIDIA pavilion at the NVIDIA Berlin GPU Technology Conference (GTC) on October 21, 2026 in Berlin, Germany. Sean Gallup | Getty Images Wall Street firm Seaport reiterated its bearish call on Nvidia with a sell rating and its price target on the stock of $180 per share, below Nvidia's Thursday closing price of $212.
 While analyst Jay Goldberg thinks the AI leader is heading into 2027 "in a good position," he's concerned about the bottleneck of the power and the overall construction of data center buildout given the lack of electricians, gas turbines and gigawatt capacity, he wrote in a Thursday research note. 
 The firm is also worried about the risk of Nvidia over taxing its balance sheet as the company added $250 billion in commitments last quarter to secure supply chain capacity and facilitate data center construction. 
 At the same time, Seaport acknowledges their take "could be wrong" as Nvidia can leverage is "supply chain heft." Shares of Nvidia were flat in pre-market trading on Friday.
 — Paulina Likos 
 8 Hours Ago Stocks open lower
 The three major indexes opened lower on Friday.
 The S&P 500 shed 0.6%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down about 1%, or 535 points. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.5%.
 — Liz Napolitano 
 8 Hours Ago Volatility index surges above 20 after gaining 14% Thursday
 Traders work in the S&P options pit at the Cboe Global Markets exchange on Sept. 16, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. Scott Olson | Getty Images The Cboe Market Volatility Index climbed another 6% Friday, rising to 20.24, after jumping 14% Thursday to 19.03.
 For the week, the VIX — widely called Wall Street's "fear gauge" — is on track to close above 20 for the first time since early June. Last week, the VIX, which measures the market's expectation of 30-day forward implied volatility based on S&P 500 index options, soared 34.7% to close at 19.99, the largest one-week gain also since early June.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon CBOE Market Volatility Index over the past six months — Scott Schnipper 
 9 Hours Ago Stocks making big moves in pre-market trading 
 Here are the stocks making the biggest moves before the bell. 
 Moderna – Shares are down 5.7% Friday morning after falling 25% on Thursday following a leak of partial data on its closely watched cancer vaccine developed with Merck . Both stocks faltered even though the full data which was released Thursday appeared meaningful for patients and positive relative to Wall Street expectations.
 Deckers – Shares of the shoemaker are down 6.7% after it reported fiscal second quarter earnings late Thursday that missed analyst expectations. Revenue for the quarter ended Sept. 30 was $1.43 billion compared to the $1.51 Wall Street was expecting. Revenue from top brands including HOKA and UGG missing FactSet expectations.
 SpaceX — Shares of the Elon Musk space and AI company were also getting a boost from an upgrade on Wall Street. PhillipCapital double upgraded the shares to buy from sell, raising its price target all the way to $250 from $75, citing surprising gains for its AI business. The new price target represents a 70% gain from here.
 Bloom Energy – Shares are down 2.5% after the energy technology solutions provider for data centers reported third quarter earnings late Thursday. Despite beating on the top and bottom line and raising its full-year 2026 earnings per share guidance, what stirred fear among investors was the reported negative free cash flow for the quarter.
 Read the full list .
 — Paulina Likos, Liz Napolitano 
 10 Hours Ago Telecommunications stocks fall as SpaceX reportedly moves toward becoming wireless carrier 
 Telecommunications stocks slid on Friday following a report that SpaceX is taking another step toward becoming a wireless carrier. 
 The Elon Musk-led company is in talks to obtain access to at least ​80,000 cell sites across the U.S., Bloomberg reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. SpaceX has discussed its plans with Crown Castle , among other cell infrastructure firms. 
 AT&T and T-Mobile US fell nearly 5% in pre-market trading, while Verizon Communications pulled back about 4%. 
 — Liz Napolitano 
 10 Hours Ago PhillipCapital hikes SpaceX to buy from sell after earnings
 Samuel Boivin | Nurphoto | Getty Images Stronger-than-expected revenue from SpaceX's AI business is making PhillipCapital — once a bear on the company — bullish about the Elon Musk giant's stock. 
 The firm upgraded shares of the space and AI company to buy from sell, and hiked its price target to $250 from $75. That level implies an almost 73% gain from Thursday's close. Analyst Glenn Thum wrote in a Friday note that the company had key catalysts driving SpaceX into a profit for the first time as a publicly-traded stock, one of them being its AI business. 
 "SI, as new cloud services agreements came online at higher rental prices and Cursor added US$608mn from mid-August," Thum said in the note, referring to the company's AI business as its branded "super intelligence" name. "Operating leverage, as higher-margin cloud services turned SI profitable."
 Shares of SpaceX were higher by 1% in premarket trading Friday. CNBC Pro subscribers can read more here . 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon SpaceX 5-day chart. — Davis Giangiulio  
 12 Hours Ago Treasury yields move higher
 Treasury yields edged higher early Friday, following a sharp drop in the previous session.
 Yields on 10-year U.S. Treasurys — the main benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — rose by 2 basis points to 4.9759%.
 The yield on the 2-year Treasury note, which more closely follows short-term Federal Reserve rate decisions, also increased by 2 basis points to 4.6625%.  The yield on longer-dated 30-year U.S. Treasurys — which tends to move on geopolitical developments — was up more than 1 basis point to 5.2985%.
 — Hugh Leask 
 13 Hours Ago Gucci-parent Kering stock plunges amid luxury slump
 A guest wears red knitted Gucci x Adidas sweater, outside Bluemarble, during the Menswear Spring/Summer 2026 show as part of Paris Fashion Week on June 26, 2025 in Paris, France. Claudio Lavenia | Getty Images Shares of Gucci-owner Kering fell 12% in early trading after the luxury company posted disappointing third-quarter earnings.
 The move puts the stock firmly at the bottom of the pan-European blue-chip Stoxx 600 index, and brings 12-month losses to 43%.
 Same-store sales declined by 1% overall, driven by a 6% decline for Gucci, its biggest brand and main moneymaker. 
 Kering, whose brands also include Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta, and Balenciaga, has struggled more than peers amid a luxury slump.
 Reigniting brand momentum at Gucci has proven particularly challenging against a difficult macroeconomic backdrop where consumers grapple with higher costs of living, Bernstein analyst Luca Solca said.
 "A high dependency on newness to drive traffic and sales points to an underlying lack of interest in Gucci's core product," Solca added. "Unsurprisingly, management has stepped back from its initial outlook of a return to growth by the end of the year."
 European luxury peers were also in the red on Friday morning, with conglomerate LVMH down 1.5%, Cartier-owner Richemont down 2.4% and Hermes falling 1.2%. 
 Hermes shares fell nearly 5% Thursday after reporting quarterly earnings, weighed down by soft demand in China.Kering
 watch now VIDEO 2:09 02:09 Kering shares plunge as Gucci continues to falter Squawk Box Europe - Elsa Ohlen 
 14 Hours Ago Asia-Pacific markets end the week mixed
 Asia-Pacific markets closed mixed on Friday.
 South Korea's benchmark Kospi index added 0.3% to 5,550.3, while the tech-heavy Kosdaq index declined 1.62% to 751.69. 
 Japan's  Nikkei 225  lost 0.34% to 62,693.16 and the broader Topix declined 0.79% to 3,965.81.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was flat at 8,795.2.
 The CSI 300 rose 1.71% to end at 4,105.33, but closed lower for the week for an 11th straight time.
 —Lee Ying Shan 
 14 Hours Ago L’Oréal sales beat forecasts as premium beauty demand picks up
 The logo of French cosmetics Groupe L'Oreal is seen on the L'Oreal group's headquarters building in Clichy, near Paris, France, April 14, 2025.  Stephanie Lecocq | Reuters Third-quarter sales at L'Oreal topped forecasts amid stronger demand for premium hair and beauty products.
 Total sales were 35.33 billion euros ($39.6 billion) for the three-month period, an adjusted like-for-like growth of 7.7% overall.
 The French cosmetics group saw a particularly strong performance in Europe, where sales rose 9%, while revenue in South Asia and the Middle East rose 19.5% in the quarter. The company also saw a slight expansion in the beauty market in China.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon L'Oreal. "The global beauty market, once again, proved its resilience in a challenging context – and we continued to significantly outpace it," said CEO Nicolas Hieronimus, highlighting strong performances across all developed regions as well as e-commerce growth in emerging markets.
 Shares were more than 3.7% higher in morning trade.
 — Domi Suskova 
 14 Hours Ago European stock market move lower in early trade
 The pan-European Stoxx 600 was down 0.19% lower shortly after 8:10 a.m. in London (3:10 a.m. E.T.) with the continent's main sectors mixed, and regional bourses moving lower.
 Oil and gas led morning gains, rising 1.24%, with household goods adding 0.56%, and bank stocks up 0.36%.
 In Frankfurt, Germany's DAX led losses, falling 0.35%.In Paris, the French CAC 40 dropped 0.18% in early dealmaking, as the U.K. FTSE 100 slipped almost 0.1% in London.
 Italy's FTSE MIB added 0.21% in Milan.
 —Hugh Leask 
 15 Hours Ago U.K. retail sales fall more than expected in September
 Street scene in Old Bond Street, Mayfair, London, United Kingdom. Pawel Libera | The Image Bank | Getty Images U.K. retail sales fell 0.4% in September from the previous month, a steeper drop than the 0.1% decline forecast in a Reuters poll. The fall partly reversed August's 0.7% rise and puts consumer spending in focus ahead of the government's budget on Oct. 28.
 Despite September's decline, retail sales volumes rose 0.7% in the third quarter from the previous three months, the Office for National Statistics said Friday.
 Phil Monkhouse, U.K. country manager at Ebury, said September's retail sales slide indicates a still-fragile consumer backdrop as households continue to grapple with rising prices and the prospect of higher borrowing costs.
  "With the Autumn Budget less than a week away, uncertainty over potential tax changes adds another layer of caution for households and businesses alike," Monkhouse said in a note.
 September's retail slide comes after U.K. GDP rose by 0.1% in August, which was driven mainly by services output.
 — Hugh Leask 
 15 Hours Ago Defense giant Saab sees orders triple after Gripen fighter jet deal with Ukraine
 Swedish defense giant Saab reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings and revenue on Friday, as new orders more than tripled from a year earlier, boosted by a deal to supply Gripen fighter jets to Ukraine.
 New orders came in at 65.8 billion Swedish kronor ($6.6 billion), up from 20.9 billion kronor a year earlier, beating FactSet expectations of 56.4 billion kronor.
 The results come as European governments race to turn defense spending pledges into military capability.
 Third-quarter sales reached 20.6 billion kronor, ahead of FactSet expectations of 20 billion kronor. Earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) came in at 1.95 billion kronor, also beating forecasts of 1.9 billion kronor.
 Saab's order intake included a 24.6 billion kronor contract for 16 Gripen E fighter jets for Ukraine, signed in June and booked in the third quarter. Deliveries are scheduled for 2029-2030.
 Read more here. 
 - Elsa Ohlen 
 16 Hours Ago Europe's stock markets set to start Friday's session in the green
 Stoxx 50 futures were up almost 0.1% ahead of the market open, with European stock markets set to start the final trading session of the week in mostly positive territory.
 The French CAC 40 was up 0.42%, following by Italy's FTSE MIB , which added 0.09%, while FTSE 100 futures were up 0.07%. 
 In contrast, Germany's DAX is seen moving 0.17% lower at the start of trade. 
 —Hugh Leask 
 17 Hours Ago SGX CEO Loh Boon Chye to step down 
 Singapore Exchange CEO Loh Boon Chye has signaled he will be stepping down as CEO, although no fixed date for a handover has been decided.
 Speaking to shareholders at SGX's AGM, Loh said that he had told chairman Koh Boon Hwee that "we should begin planning ahead for an eventual transition in the CEO role."
 Although Loh said that there was no fixed date for a handover, he noted that his contract runs till the middle of 2027, which would be an "ample time for us to plan thoughtfully and work through the arrangements together. We are not setting a specific date for the transition today."
 Loh has been SGX's chief since 2015, and Koh had said that under the CEO, the share price of the SGX has grown 216% since the time that he took the helm. 
 "Our net profit after tax is up 112%, and the market capitalization of the SGX Group is up 252%. That is a significant track record."
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 18 Hours Ago China's benchmark CSI 300 extends slide, set for 11 straight weekly drop
 China's benchmark CSI 300 deepened its slide into bear market territory on Friday, falling 0.5%.
 The index, which tracks 300 of the largest stocks listed in Shanghai and Shenzhen, is set to clock its 11th consecutive weeks of decline, down 3.5%, underscoring sustained pressure on Chinese equities, data from LSEG showed.
 Some market watchers see opportunities emerging from the sell-off, saying that much of the bad news surrounding China's economy has already been priced into stocks.
 "China's vast underperformance provides an opportunity for investors as the 'bad news' is largely well known and reflected in prices," said Brendan Ahern, chief investment officer at KraneShares.
— Lee Ying Shan 
 19 Hours Ago India says trade deal with EU could be operational by March 2027 
 The trade deal between India and the European Union is expected to be signed before the end of 2026 and become operational by March next year , India's Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday.
 The minister said it was the "fastest trade deal" the EU has entered into, "with zero dissent," adding that none of the bloc's 27 member states have opposed any part of the agreement. 
 India's free trade deal with the EU, which represents about 25% of global GDP and about a third of global trade, was announced in January. It had been in the works for over two decades.
 Just days after India finalized the agreement with the EU, U.S. President Donald Trump also announced a trade deal with India . 
 U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday said Washington would execute a deal with India "shortly," and there were just a "small number of items left to wrap up."
 19 Hours Ago SK Hynix scraps Solidigm IPO plans; shares slightly lower in choppy trade 
 Shares of South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix pared early losses to trade slightly lower on Friday after the company halted a review of a potential U.S. initial public offering for its subsidiary Solidigm.
 Shares in Seoul had dropped over 3% early morning, while they had declined 8% in the U.S. overnight.
 "Solidigm will halt its review of potential pre-IPO and IPO options," the company said in the statement after assessing recent capital market conditions and share price trends, while also exploring various funding options to finance a new U.S. semiconductor fabrication plant amid growing demand for AI memory.
 The chip manufacturer said an IPO could have helped fund Solidigm's expansion while providing greater financial flexibility for shareholder returns, including dividends and share buybacks.
 However, financial market volatility has increased, contributing to a broader correction in semiconductor stocks, prompting SK Hynix to reassess whether an IPO would benefit existing shareholders.
 — Ying Shan Lee and Jenny Lee 
 Correction: This post has been revised to reflect that shares in the U.S. fell 8%. 
 21 Hours Ago Japan core inflation in September surges to its highest this year at 2.1%
 Japan's core inflation in September hit its highest this year at 2.1%, overshooting analysts' expectations, pressured by steeper import costs due to a weak yen and the indirect impact of higher energy costs.
 Core inflation, which strips out prices of fresh food, was in line with the 2.1% forecast by economists polled by Reuters, and accelerated from the 1.7% in the prior month.
 Headline inflation came in at 2.1%, while the so-called "core-core" inflation, which excludes prices of fresh food and energy and is the Bank of Japan's preferred gauge, was at 2.4%.
 "That acceleration was noteworthy, not least because it occurred despite a sharp slowdown in fresh food inflation and continued energy deflation," said Abhijit Surya, senior APAC economist at Capital Economics.
 Rice prices notably declined 20.6% year on year, however, Surya said that this sharp drop could not prevent overall goods inflation from picking up to 2.8%, up from August's 2.6%.
 —Lim Hui Jie 
 22 Hours Ago South Korea stocks lead declines as Asia markets open lower
 Asia-Pacific markets fell on Friday, with South Korean equities leading declines in the region.
 The benchmark Kospi index fell 2.42%, while the tech-heavy Kosdaq index declined 2.6%.
 Japan's  Nikkei 225  lost 0.49% and the broader Topix declined 0.86%.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was 0.21% lower.
 —Lee Ying Shan 
 22 Hours Ago Asia-Pacific markets set to fall, tracking Wall Street losses on AI concerns
 Asia-Pacific markets were set to mostly fall on Friday, tracking losses on Wall Street as concerns over soaring artificial intelligence spending and surging oil prices weighed on investor sentiment.
 Futures for Japan's  Nikkei 225  in Chicago were at 62,360 while in Osaka they were last at 62,310 compared with the index's previous close of 62,907.84.
 Futures for Hong Kong's Hang Seng index last traded at 23,133, compared with the index's last close of 22,934.68.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was down 0.34% in early trading.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 23 Hours Ago Stocks making the biggest moves in after hours: Western Digital, Bloom Energy & more
 Several stocks saw dramatic swings in extended trading following another raft of quarterly reports.
 Western Digital — Shares of the data storage company fell 5%. The decline came after hard selling in the artificial intelligence trade during the regular session. Separately, Western Digital posted fiscal first quarter results that exceeded estimates, with adjusted earnings of $4.64 per share trouncing the LSEG consensus call for $4.09 per share. Revenue of $4.38 billion beat the expected $4.14 billion. 
 Bloom Energy — The fuel cell power company fell 5% even as third-quarter results trounced analysts' estimates. Adjusted earnings of 94 cents per share and revenue of $1.24 billion surpassed the LSEG consensus call for 68 cents per share and $1.06 billion. Guidance for full-year revenues and adjusted earnings also came in ahead of estimates.
 Read more about Thursday's big movers in extended trading here .
 — Darla Mercado 
 24 Hours Ago Sliding bond yields Thursday lift homebuilders, banks and REITs
 The largest one-day decline since March 2023 in the 10-year Treasury note yield Thursday helped drive up the value of homebuilders, banks and real estate investment trusts. 
 The State Street SPDR S&P Homebuilders ETF surged 3.8%, the State Street SPDR S&P Regional Banking ETF rallied 2.5% and the Vanguard Real Estate ETF added 1.3% — all of them handily outperforming the S&P 500, which dropped 1.2%.
 — Scott Schnipper 
 24 Hours Ago U.S. stock futures open little changed after tech rout
 U.S. stock futures were little changed as trading began at 6 p.m. in New York.
 Dow futures advanced 38 points, or 0.07%, while S&P 500 futures gained 0.05%. Nasdaq-100 futures slipped 0.07%.
 — Darla Mercado
